verdict.tagline: A sprawling industrial puzzle that rewards patience beyond a punishing start.
for_you_if: you love deep industrial automation and planetary logistics
you can push through a steep opening learning curve
you enjoy scaling massive factory builds over dozens of hours
not_for_you_if: you need a smooth tutorial to learn complex mechanics
you want native cooperative multiplayer with friends
you expect robust controller support and clean interface scaling
you require cloud saves to protect your progress across systems

distortion_flags.sentence: Player approval scales upward as reviewers progress past the opening hours.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early hours feature steep friction with un-intuitive controls, missing controller support, and tiny user interface text.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as clunky, un-intuitive, and difficult to grasp at the start.

citations.review_text: As a big fan of factory/automation games, I couldn't ignore this one and the overwhelmingly positive reviews...but my god, this software is just a nightmare to engage with. After configuring the UI to make it readable, it often remains indecipherable. Placing buildings/conveyers/sorters is so finicky and unintuitive, I couldn't believe it. With the existence of Satisfactory, StarRupture, and Factorio, I would only recommend this game to a factory fiend that already has hundreds of hours in those games.

To be honest, I don't know how these early access games end up with Overwhelmingly Positive reviews. This one is so clunky and unintuitive from the get go. It takes a while just to figure out the basics, how to connect buildings, what the upgrades actually do and how to apply them, and what all the different systems do. After coming from a game like Satisfactory or Planet Crafter, this one is something you want to love because it initially looks and feels cool, but can quickly get frustrating. I'm sure with more time, and hours spent reading forums, it'll be fun and interesting, but I'm not there yet and seems like it might be a very long time until I feel that way. No built-in multiplayer is also a huge turn off.

Seems neat on its face. I wanted to like it. The gameplay is just too slow and clunky. A few hours in, and I can't imagine investing the time into playing a game to completion. Maybe I'll come back to it when I hit a nursing home or something.

I don't get it? I hate to be a critic - I LOVE building, automation and space, this seemed like a sure deal for me. 

I think the translation barrier is difficult to get over, and it's just too much. Too many processes, nothing is intuitive like it should be. Factorio was easier than this. 

It's beautiful, maybe it's good for you, but it just didn't stick for me, and I've bought it twice.

poor grammar translations and a LOT of manual crafting early game, i refunded it the second i began getting into the actual game because of how overcomplicated this is, i would prefer factorio or satisfactory over this anyday

claims.claim: Blueprint copying and pasting features fail by reversing designs, misaligning structures, or omitting conveyor belts.

citations.review_text:
I am completely hooked to this game. Even though it is an early access title, I think it is pretty much a complete game. 

I would like to say that I am a complete disaster in terms of doing a really structured base, as it is shown in the game trailer and maybe from some skilled people. Mine is completely ♥♥♥♥ and chaos, with no good planning whatsoever. Nevertheless, it is rewarding to gradually unlock more things, improve your base, produce new things and so on. And ultimately, expanding to the other planets - which is fascinating. I think whoever liked Factorio or Satisfactory would also love this game.

What I like:
* Factory game with not so complicated (for now) tower defence
* Possibility of expanding to the stars with new biomes and possibilities
* Adequate graphics that fits with the concept of the game
* Being completely sandbox with relaxing progress

What I dont like:
*placement of the extractors to the mining nodes. That sucks. I am able to replicate items with my mecha robot but not being able to extract a mining node a pixel away :/
*different outlets and inlets of the factories/storage facilities is sometimes tiresome. it is not hard, but rather unsatisfactory to have to do that while ever expanding
*sometimes copying the blueprint and pasting it for pre-defined factory network does not work, and I am even having troubles of setting the initial blueprint.

This game has everything to be a very good one, just like Factorio but in 3D and a very nice alternative universe. Dyson Sphere Program is a true factory game, unlike Satisfactory which is just so bad as a factory game that it cannot be used as a comparison reference. 

In Dyson Sphere Program I like the overall gameplay, it gives a taste of positive originality, the conveyors belts system is nicely designed, the stacking of buildings is an interesting feature and overall it is easy to take in hand. Interplanertary travel is nice to have, the battle mode is satisfying and Icarus idea is great! 

But too many bugs are still existing, especially in the copy-paste of blueprints: when you paste something but half of the blueprint design is reversed or buildings are not spaced exactly like in the blueprint, or it lacks coveyors belts or other stuffs probably not randomly but without any comprehensive explaination, it is just not acceptable. Thoroughness is required to be happy building a factory, if you need to correct manually thousands of mistakes done by the game, it is just awful. I also despise the unfortunately approximate design of the planet grids and building space occupancy, which does not match the building’s visual appearance. 

Well, despite all of this, I really like this game and I am pleased to have paid for it to sustain its development, but for now I just cannot recommend it because of small bugs that give the player a bad experience once you reach a certain point of factory growth.

Dyson Sphere Program is a watered-down version of Factorio with shinier (notice I didn't say [i]better[/i]) graphics and worse gameplay. In the factory builder genre of games, tight control and strong gameplay loops are everything. Dyson Sphere Program seems to eternally frustrate this through weird, unacknowledged building rules and poor game design choices:

* Assemblers can be placed next to belts, and inserters can be connected from said belt to the machine. Stockpiles can do the same. Despite this, assemblers and stockpiles have weird hitboxes, and cannot be placed next to each-other, making direct insertion (say as in a mall) impossible without reduced throughput. Weirdly, you can place a belt between them and [i]two[/i] inserters, and get full speed.
* If you run a belt over another belt, and then need to interact with the belt on the bottom, you need to delete the belt over top to do so.
* If you try to place an inserter on a belt corner, you can't, and instead must stretch it out a tile to get to another straight piece. Despite this, if the inserter is already placed [i]before[/i] you build the elbow, it'll pick up and put down on the curved part just fine. I shouldn't have to cheese the building system like this. Consistency is important - either make it work all of the time or none of the time.
* Blueprints don't recognize already-placed structures on the ground, so you can't tile a pattern or complete a partially built blueprint without hitting the force button, which won't show conflicts.
* Belts running over other belts need a certain amount of "runway" on each side to build, and can't turn sharply. Despite this, if you just add a sharp turn belt after it's already built, it works perfectly.
* Dark Fog adds nothing to the game. The narrative elements are thin and enemy variety is minimal. Feels like a "well factorio had biters, I guess we need an enemy" - devs failed to realize that the enemy is already the clunky building system.
* Belt tilt. …

claims.claim: Refineries output mixed resources onto the same conveyor belt despite correct filter settings, causing production lines to clog.

citations.review_text: I really like the game. The problem I have is that some basic functions are a bit bugged and at this point, should have been fixed. First encountered this bug on the refinery, output hydrogen/refined oil onto two separate belts. The filters are set correctly. Will still occasionally output both resources onto the same belt, clogging production. The combat is enjoyable, very similar to games like factorio. Drip fed updates, although I don't fault the devs as this is a pretty ambitious game that ties into a milky way system of other players reporting power generated. I don't recommend this game in its current state after 5 years. Deep sale? Probably.

claims.claim: The tutorial prompts the player with text hints and instructions that disappear after a single presentation without verifying whether the task was completed.

citations.review_text:
This game is wildly unfriendly to interface with. 

The controls are rather unorthodox to a factory game veteran, but not so alien that it makes the game unplayable.
Navigating the ui is generally clunky and requires way too many button clicks and key presses just to find what is needed for a basic task.
The first hour will spam you with hints like "press WASD to move" and two seconds later "by the way you can right click to move!" and then later "And you can hold shift right click to queue up actions independent from your character's origin!"
The game will also spam you with readable tutorials that are far too wordy.

Compare this to a game like Factorio which only teaches the basic concepts needed to play. It leaves the player to discover all the tech like holding shift or ctrl while crafting to make different amounts of an item, or pressing are while belting to rotate your belt line instantly.

Of course comparing a pioneer of the genre to an early access game is a bit absurd. I would just like the devs to put time into reducing friction for new players interfacing with the many complex systems of the game.

After spending more time hashing out the gameplay I'm going change my review to a recommend.  The game has a lot of dept and starts to become a lot of fun once you know what you are doing.  I have a couple of suggestions on how to improve the new player experience if the developers actually read this.

#1 The tutorial isn't great and I think the biggest problem for me is that you give verbal explanations one time with no verification the player was able to complete a task.   I think verbal explanations should persist until the player actually accomplishes the task and potentially add visual ques for people that are visual learner such as myself.   In particular I couldn't figure out how to connect buildings without going to an external source.  Coming from satisfactory and alchemy factory having never played factorio I'm used to belts connecting directly to buildings so the concept of having to use a sorter to connect things was very foreign and unintuitive.   It isn't terribly complicated once you understand it, but I don't think its intuitive at all. The game really needs to do a better job with this concept.

#2 The AI should be automatically disabled for new players imo or it shouldn't attack until the player has researched and built its first defense.  I'd even got a step further and say the first attack should be part of the tutorial which tells you build defense and then the first attack is kind of scripted.   I very nearly quit playing the game because when my first attack came in I had no defense and no way to defend myself and it was game over.   Pretty frustrating in a building game when you are trying to learn and something like that happens.  So I'd say either AI off be default make the player turn it on so someone isn't trying to learn and then have game over because of this or make the first attack scripted so the player is somewhat ready when it comes in.

Other than that seems like a beautiful game with a lot of depth, but I think the new player exp…

citations.review_text:
I played Factorio and Satisfactory before Dyson Sphere Program, there are just some things that are heavily lacking in QoL and progression in DSP.

Doesn't personally itch the same neural centers as the other automation games, you have to resign to always use the wiki on a second tab just to play this game normally. And the UI is just bloated with information that frankly will scare you for the first few hours.

For a game thats been in EA for 5 years, and the last major content update being 3 years ago? The game might as well tell you its basically finished and it has no plans to enhance anything of the sort.

Definitely the weakest of the big three automation games, maybe it was a mistake playing this over shapez 2. Not my cup of tea, and is less polished than the other two.

If I had played Dyson Sphere Program before Satisfactory or Factorio I'd probably be giving it a positive review. It has that same automation hooks that tickle the programmer part of my brain. But after 6 hours I'm just finding myself missing all of the quality of life improvements that Satisfactory and Factorio have.

Seeing as how Dyson Sphere Program has been in "early access" for 5 years now the game feels like it is basically in its finished state. I've resigned myself to the fact that I need to keep dsp-wiki.com open at all times and must hear "insufficient materials" every 15 seconds because the concept of "ghost" construction will never exist.

[b]**UPDATE**[/b] I played the game for 10 more hours, following a guide to try and get a good starter logistics base going. Eventually I began dealing with refined oil and  unfortunately didn’t leave enough space to expand my production line. That’s when I realized there was no straight forward way to relocate 30,000 units of liquid. You just gotta drain it all to another set of tanks, move the old ones, and then drain back which will easily take at least 30 minutes.

This is DSP in a nutshell. For every minute I enjoy the game, there are several minutes of fighting the controls and systems. There is a great game here but it is just bogged down so much that I’m not sure I can continue.

claims.claim: The game freezes or hangs on launch and struggles with settings menus.

citations.review_text: The game hangs on launch unlike many others. I've reinstalled it. The GPU drivers were released in June (it is August now). Nothing I can do to fix it. I could get to the options screen once. And even then the game froze after changing some settings and that's the end of it.

Don't buy the game until they fix the text size and ui screens disappearing.  If they could only find a way to make the text larger it would be a fun game.  I can't read anything without squinting and i am playing on a 40 inch screen tv which is a few meters away from me.  Can you figure out a way to make the text get much larger than you currently have the limit for?  I know you can lower the pixels in the ui and it makes the text go from microscopic to ultra small at best.  I want to see BIG letters on the screen.  I tried going into the options file in Documents to change the pixel height to 540 which is the best and most readable text size but then i started running into issues with screens getting cut off or when i move them with the mouse and let go of the mouse button the screen disappears and never comes back until you restart the game.  Don't get me wrong, what I played of the game was awesome but the text size issue makes it suck drastically.  Until they fix this, DON'T BUY THE GAME!!!  When they fix it, I assume it will be a masterpiece.

claims.claim: Interplanetary and planet navigation feels clumsy or tedious, involving long periods of cruise control and collisions with environment objects.

citations.review_text:
60-Hour Review: Brilliant Automation Ruined by Tedious Travel

Quick Review
Unfortunately, the interplanetary navigation completely ruins what starts as a fantastic experience. In my last four hours of gameplay, I spent more time staring at a black screen and chasing a blue line in cruise control than actually building. The travel mechanics aggressively drag down an otherwise great game

Detail

Graphics: 10/10 (Excellent)
Visually stunning. The scale of the game and the celestial views are top-notch.

Automation: 7/10 (Good)
Solid recipe challenges and great assembly combinations. There is a really satisfying balance between advancing your technology tree and scaling up your research cube production.

For me, automation games are all about the mid-to-late game: refactoring layouts, rebalancing complex supply chains, squeezing out every ounce of efficiency, and building a factory that looks neat, tidy, and organized.

There is loads of scope , faster conveyors , mods , sorters and combiners - good ticks in boxes

Planet Navigation: 3/10 (Frustrating)
Moving around on a planet feels incredibly clumsy. Constantly colliding with environment objects, fighting the flight controls, and trying to take off actually made me feel a bit motion-sick.

Interplanetary Navigation: 0/10 (Boring & Tedious)
A complete momentum killer. By the mid-game, you are forced to spend a massive amount of time traveling through deep space. It amounts to spending minutes at a time wrestling with the throttle, pitch, yaw, and cruise control just to get from point A to point B.

26.8 hours in one week. Yeah, it's that good.

Honestly didn't expect to get this hooked. The building just feels right - nothing clunky, nothing frustrating, it all clicks. And the progression keeps pulling you forward. Then at some point you unlock the ability to fly to other planets and I'm harvesting hydrogen from a gas giant like... wow.

It's not always 100% obvious what does what - I got confused between planetary and interstellar logistics systems and had to Google it. Small thing, but worth knowing going in.

If you've played Satisfactory and loved it, just buy this. I actually think it's better, but that's just my opinion. No bugs, no crashes, runs smooth as butter. Just a really solid game all round.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the initial suit power management and early game fuel requirements can leave the player stranded during space flight.

citations.review_text: it's just not very interesting, is it? same royalty free 15-second loop soundtrack forever, infinite tutorials, ai voice "information" that is actually just keybind alerts, takes forever to get anywhere, have to fuel the player character (let me just manage one power system for my factory if the entirety of the system is 'feed me fuel' with no water management or any form of actually interesting power management ala satisf or factorio). disappointed everytime i boot up with no QOL, keybinds, ghost construction, or updates. 5 years early access and every few months i pull it up to see if anything new has arrived, and nothing ever has. this is abandonware and probably mines crypto in your PC when you leave it on in the background. do not by this on some paltry 20% off. only actively supported or published games should be purchased. I'd say go get this game for free somewhere.

It is a good factory building game. I enjoyed playing through it and even through I prefer satisfactory and factorio space over it, it is a good expereince. I find the enemies to be balanced around certain overpowered strategies which makes them not that interesting to engage with (missile turrents + signal towers). Due to how you can route belts on many different layers builds become very messy, it also make it a lot more difficuilt to automate building compared to satisfactory (building take parts) or factorio where you can have requester chests stock multiple of the same item. Unlike in factorio which makes automating building that take 4 items a pain since the chest are the same size as the constructor. I think there is hidden content related to the enemies but this isn't detailed in game so I didn't explore it, this should probably be addressed. Dyson spheres (strucutre componets) feel like they take a long time to setup and produce in a reasonable capacity I feel like there needs to easier to make earlier, in a similar vein swarms should probably be moved forwards a little. In a similar capacity accumulators discharge / charge rates feel to small compared to the magnitudes of power draw in the later game so a MK2 could be a good thing to add. Early game power generation in the suit for space flight is a annoying thing at least until you get fuel rods as it is easy to run out of fuel and get stuck in space, this alongside with the controls being uninitive. It would be nice if pilesorters and similar had a hold mode to only output there max stack size (like factorio stack inserters). Currently I didn't really feel like doing much in the post-game as there wasn't really anything meaningful to work towards really outside of having to constantly go out and build more resource mining stations which I just felt as kind of a chore unlike in factorio where infinite mining productive makes it partically a non issue it feels the infiinite upgrades in their feasiable leve…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that certain game mechanics, item interactions, and instructions are unclear or non-intuitive to understand.

citations.review_text: There are things missing from onboarding and there are settings that are non-intuitively named but the game is awesome and it's still in development.

So many systems, so very little in the way of clear instructions on how they work.
I'm all for figuring out how to build and optimize systems, but when they don't even give you a clear idea of how they things you get work, it's a bit... annoying.

Now I'm not saying the instruction are not there... just that at times they are clear as MUD.

26.8 hours in one week. Yeah, it's that good.

Honestly didn't expect to get this hooked. The building just feels right - nothing clunky, nothing frustrating, it all clicks. And the progression keeps pulling you forward. Then at some point you unlock the ability to fly to other planets and I'm harvesting hydrogen from a gas giant like... wow.

It's not always 100% obvious what does what - I got confused between planetary and interstellar logistics systems and had to Google it. Small thing, but worth knowing going in.

If you've played Satisfactory and loved it, just buy this. I actually think it's better, but that's just my opinion. No bugs, no crashes, runs smooth as butter. Just a really solid game all round.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as running smoothly with good performance and optimization.

citations.review_text:
I really like this game. It's very fun! spending hours building factories and learning new stuff the tutorial hasn't caught up to yet is fun. It makes my laptop run kind of hot, but it runs wonderfully, even during combat!!

Negatives ------ This game needs a progress loader before the loading progress loader. seems asinine, but I thought the game was broken.. It just needs about 5 minutes for my slower SSD drives to load the game fully. If you are on a Physical Hard Drive Disk prepare to wait a while for it to open!

I’ll be honest: when I first bought this game, I expected it to be a lesser version of Factorio or Satisfactory. I thought it couldn't possibly live up to those titans of the automation genre.
Dyson Sphere Program absolutely blew me away. The sheer scale of building factory lines across entire planets, solar systems, and galaxies is mind-boggling. The progression feels incredibly rewarding, the optimization is smooth, and visually, it is stunning to look at.
If you love automation games and think you've seen it all, give this one a chance. It’s not just a clone; it’s a masterpiece that stands proudly right alongside the best in the genre.
10/10 - Absolutely highly recommended!

claims.claim: The game lacks native cloud saves, resulting in lost save files and blueprints if systems are reinstalled or drives are changed.

citations.review_text:
Love this game so much. Didn't think about it when I was trying to move the game to a different drive, but they don't do steam cloud saves and I lost all my blueprints and save files. I'm more upset about the blueprints since I made them from scratch. I know it's my fault for not saving a backup for the save files and blueprints, but it still sucks so bad.

BACKUP YOUR SAVES AND BLUEPRINTS

Extraordinarily fun game when you finally get to build a sphere and see it from a close planet.
Tiny install size, runs extremely well, but.... no cloud saves!? I lost my 150+ hour save due to a system reinstall, and not knowing that the saves are local only..

claims.claim: The game experiences performance chugging and lag on busy planets and in the endgame as calculations scale up.

citations.review_text:
Hard to believe this is early access. Frankly this is a complete game in the state it's in.


However there are optimizations needed especially in endgame. I have an RTX 5090, and a 12900k, 96gb 6400 ram. And this game will still chug on busy planets, or even anywhere if you have enough happening at once.

Thankfully there are mods, especially SphereOpt (Basically makes Dyson spheres a non factor for performance), DSPOptimizations, and Weaver all can make a huge difference.

Excited to see what the devs add, and hope the incorporate the optimizations these mods make.

Absolutely fantastic game, I've spent a looooong time playing this. The game is in Early Access, but it feels complete already. The devs keep adding new things - big and small. Recently, they changed the optimisation in the game and it made late-game feel much better as previously, the amount of calculations made it very laggy. Prior to that, they added combat against the Dark Fog. They're very passionate devs and I was motivated to post this review as I saw a recent review saying "Game seems abandoned, it's still in EA". This is fundamentally not the case. It still gets updates and patches and as I said, there's enough there that it feels complete already! An update was posted on January 21, 2026 which specifically stated that they are working on a vehicle update along with space stations which will be launched together. This is the final major update prior to the official release. 

If you're interested in this and aren't sure about your hardware, I'd suggest that CPU is more important than GPU. It'll be running a lot of calculations on a huge number of things as you progress and you'll need the processing power to manage these

Very, very good game. Very addictive. Has tons of content and I enjoyed it very very much. Looking forward for additions in the future. It's already pretty good. Yeah, its missing some QOL, like navigation line to finished miner and its getting quite choppy in the end-game. But to be honest, it does not deminish my enjoyment from the game in general.
I LOVE the game. the only complaint that I have is at my point with my specs the game is a lagy but that only because of my low specs
Can run a decent size factory on a very old PC, it does chug at times though.
